paragraphs: Spare sells operations software that a public transit agency runs its service on. The modes it covers include paratransit, microtransit and fixed route, along with asset management.

In one system an agency handles scheduling and dispatch, the rider experience, fleet health, and compliance and reporting. Because paratransit trips are often contracted out, the platform pulls trips from different providers into one place. Eligibility applications and rider records are digitized, which the company says speeds up the review process. On the fixed route side, an agency can plan service, publish a GTFS feed, build schedules and run live operations together. A voice assistant answers rider calls for bookings, arrival times and common questions.

The platform is described as built to meet ADA, NTD and grant reporting requirements. It connects through open APIs, GTFS, AVL feeds and single sign-on rather than replacing what a technology team already runs. Spare puts its reach at more than 230 communities. Its fixed route page describes coordinating a large event shuttle for LA Metro.

quote.text: Built for ADA, NEMT, and compliance complexity.
